name: Dima and Sequence
description: Dima got into number sequences. Now he's got sequence a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n , consisting of n positive integers. Also, Dima has got a function f ( x ) , which can be defined with the following recurrence: f (0) = 0 ; f (2· x ) = f ( x ) ; f (2· x + 1) = f ( x ) + 1 . Dima wonders, how many pairs of indexes ( i , j ) (1 ≤ i < j ≤ n ) are there, such that f ( a i ) = f ( a j ) . Help him, count the number of such pairs.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) . The second line contains n positive integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ) . The numbers in the lines are separated by single spaces.
output_specification: In a single line print the answer to the problem. Please, don't use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in C++ . It is preferred to use the cin , cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 272B — Dima and Sequence [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
